title: Neo Turf Masters
subtitle: Golf at an arcade pace
summary: Neo Turf Masters is Nazca's golf game, first released for Neo Geo arcades on 29 January 1996.
body: Neo Turf Masters is Nazca's golf game, first released for Neo Geo arcades on 29 January 1996. Known in Japan as Big Tournament Golf, it offers six golfers and four fictional courses associated with the United States, Japan, Australia and Germany. The presentation gives each shot a quick, clear sequence rather than a lengthy simulation. Stroke play supports one or two players, while match play provides a direct two-player contest. Nazca released it shortly before Metal Slug, showing another side of the studio's ability to make arcade action immediately approachable.

The shot system separates power from height. One input sets the strength of the swing, and another determines how high the ball will travel, while hook and slice are selected beforehand. That arrangement makes the controls quick to learn, leaving the course and wind to provide much of the difficulty. A promising line can become unreliable when the conditions change. The player must connect the visible landing area with the chosen club, trajectory and wind, then carry out the short timing sequence that turns the plan into a shot.

The golfers' differing attributes give another choice before the round begins, while the four courses vary the situations those strengths must address. Hazards and demanding layouts keep a simple swing system from making the competition predictable. Takushi Hiyamuta composed the music, contributing to its bright arcade atmosphere. Later releases often used the Japanese title Big Tournament Golf. The original's appeal lies in how quickly it reaches the meaningful part of the sport: assess the next stretch of ground, judge the conditions and see whether a precisely timed swing can deliver the intended result.
